_id: scene008 with the Monte-Carlo consistency ensemble run at the FULL 3600 s arc instead of the 900 s default. This is the REFERENCE half of the pair whose other half is feat025mc: the two differ in estimation.multipathBias.useInEKF and in nothing else, so the difference in the NEES verdict is attributable to the multipath error model alone.
_delta: report.monteCarlo.enable true (was false) and duration_s 3600 (golden_baseline ships 900). nSeeds 12 and confidence 0.99 inherited unchanged.
_WHYTHISRUNGEXISTS: The frozen Final sweep has validationStatisticsNeesEnable = 0 and monteCarloStatus = notRun on every rung, so neesPositionMean is NaN and neesPositionStatus is notAvailable. The state-covariance question R-SA-P-020 asks therefore has NO evidence behind it anywhere in the sweep. NIS is a measurement-side statistic and is silent about it. This rung and feat025mc supply that evidence for the one lever that is expected to move it.
_WHYNOTTHE900sDEFAULT: MonteCarloConsistency uses burnInFraction 0.5, which is NOT exposed through cfg.report.monteCarlo. At the 900 s default it pools epochs 451-900 and at 3600 s it pools 1801-3600. The converged metric this chapter reports is the last 20 percent of a 3600 s arc, so a 900 s ensemble would band-check a transient and attach the verdict to a converged number. Same reasoning as best002mc.
_REGRESSIONCHECK: MonteCarloConsistency runs AFTER the main pipeline and cannot reach back into it, so the main arc here must reproduce scene008 exactly: posRMS_tail20pct 1.5233 m. If it does not, something other than the MC block moved and the pair is void.
